chosen.premise: Mankey gets angry when separated from its group, then gets angrier when its rampage makes everyone leave.
chosen.hook: Mankey’s rage creates the exact loneliness that fuels it.
chosen.visualIdea: Animate Mankey losing its group, rampaging, watching everyone flee, and becoming even angrier.
chosen.note: A distinctive self-reinforcing emotional loop: separation causes rage, rage drives everyone away, and loneliness intensifies the rage. Both halves are explicitly supported.

candidates.premise: Mankey’s rage tires it into sleep, but angry dreams wake it up and restart the rampage.
candidates.hook: Mankey can literally wake up angry from an angry dream.
candidates.visualIdea: Loop between raging, collapsing asleep, dreaming angrily, and jolting awake furious again.
candidates.note: Highly memorable and unusually specific, with a clean visual loop. It relies on one entry, but that entry directly supports the entire premise.

candidates.premise: One enraged Mankey can make its entire treetop colony rampage for no reason.
candidates.hook: Mankey anger is contagious—and silence is almost impossible.
candidates.visualIdea: Show one Mankey flashing red, then anger spreading through a treetop colony like a shockwave.
candidates.note: A concrete colony-wide mechanic, directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries. Slightly less surprising because contagious group anger is a familiar Mankey trait.

candidates.premise: Mankey visibly shakes and breathes roughly before rage, but the warning arrives too late to escape.
candidates.hook: Mankey gives you a warning—but not enough time to run.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom in on shaking fur and rough nasal breathing, then cut instantly to an unstoppable attack.
candidates.note: The warning-that-is-too-late contradiction is concrete and well supported, though less novel than Mankey’s broader rage-cycle behavior.

candidates.premise: Mankey’s inability to hold in stress may help it live a long time, despite losing its temper constantly.
candidates.hook: Mankey’s worst personality trait might be its survival strategy.
candidates.visualIdea: Contrast a calm Pokémon bottling stress with Mankey instantly exploding, then reveal the longevity claim.
candidates.note: The longevity claim is directly stated, but the survival-strategy framing is an interpretation rather than a firmly established mechanism. It also needs careful wording to avoid implying real-world medical causation.

candidates.premise: Mankey’s evolution path turns its Fighting identity into a Fighting/Ghost final form after a move is used.
candidates.hook: Mankey’s evolution ends with its rage becoming a Ghost type.
candidates.visualIdea: Build the chain Mankey to Primeape at level 28, then reveal Annihilape’s new Ghost typing after using a move.
candidates.note: The evolution and typing facts are supported, but the claim that rage becomes Ghost typing is thematic interpretation, not something the research establishes.
